analysis:
Single added file: provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Live/PrefixQualification/ModelCheckpointRestoreContentionLiveTests.swift (lines 1-261). It is an opt-in live test and is disabled unless DARKBLOOM_RESTORE_CONTENTION_BENCHMARK=1. It also requires DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_EXCLUSIVE_GPU=1 and a new absolute output path. It is test-only code and does not alter production gating, TTL, HMAC lookup, DBK3 AAD, coordinator scope derivation, or any other T-041 affected file. No attestation, authorization, billing or WebSocket behavior is touched.

Security-relevant observations, none of which is a finding:
- It exercises SSD restore across distinct per-condition tenant scopes (lines 101, 143), consistent with the T-041 salt-scoping mitigation. It does not assert cross-scope isolation, so it is not a regression test for cross-tenant leakage.
- It deliberately measures the restore vs cold TTFT, which is the SEC-035 timing-oracle class. The report written by Report.save (lines 47-51) contains timing, token counts, modelID, weightHash and build/runtime info. It contains no prompt content or keys. Prompts come from ModelCheckpointStoragePrompts, defined in another file and not reviewed here.
- The output path is user-supplied via environment variable. Writes are atomic and the path must not already exist, though the check-then-write is racy. This is acceptable for a developer test.
- It uses @testable and the @_spi(Benchmarking) import of ProviderCore. I did not review whether the SPI surface is compiled into production; that is outside the supplied evidence.

No threat model update appears necessary. A later pass could check that the benchmark SPI APIs (ModelPrefixBenchmarkFixture, session.drainCheckpointWrites) are not reachable from production builds.
